subject: Mariner Health - Private/VPC discovery recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@marinerhealth.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@marinerhealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Mariner Health - Private/VPC discovery recap

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the quick call today. Per our conversation, below is a short recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Key pain points you shared:
- Regulated patient data (PHI) requires VPC deployment and strict network egress controls.
- Customer-managed KMS for key isolation and auditability.
- Occasional need for air-gapped model updates in closed environments.
- Need predictable SLAs and capacity for nightly batch inference jobs.

Current stack & constraints:
- On-prem Kubernetes (AKS/VMware) with strict outbound firewall rules; only specific IP ranges allowed.
- Primary data store in a private VPC; no public S3 access for certain buckets.
- Security/compliance team requires SOC 2 + encryption-in-transit and at-rest with KMS integration.

Success criteria for PoC:
1) Private/VPC deployment (customer VPC peering or managed VPC) with no PHI leaving the network.
2) Integration with your KMS (HSM-backed keys preferred).
3) Demonstrate end-to-end inference for a sample PHI dataset with latency and throughput targets for 100 concurrent sessions.
4) Documented operational runbook and evidence for audit (logs, key access events).

Risks & open questions:
- Air-gap workflow: how frequently will you accept model updates and what format for secure transfer?
- Specific KMS provider/version and whether HSM is required for the PoC.
- Network team will need a detailed list of required IP ranges and ports for approval.

Next steps (proposed):
- Marissa/Redwood: share a short Private/VPC overview + required network egress matrix (attached).
- Mariner Health: share a network diagram and KMS provider details (we sent a template XLSX request attached).
- Schedule technical deep-dive with your infra team (Dylan to join) — propose Wed 03/10 or Thu 03/11.

Attachments: redwood-private-overview.pdf (overview + deployment options), mariner-network-diagram-request.xlsx (template for network/KMS details).
Meeting recording: https://drive.google.com/meeting-recording-20260303

If that all looks right I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the infra deep-dive.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mariner Health - Private/VPC discovery recap

Thanks Marissa — great recap and captures everything we discussed. A few clarifications from the Mariner infra/security side: 

- KMS: We use AWS KMS with CloudHSM for higher-sensitivity keys. HSM-backed keys are a requirement for any production deployment.
- Air-gap cadence: model updates are quarterly for regulated pipelines; however, we will need the ability to apply emergency patches outside that cadence (secured transfer over an approved channel).
- Network: our security team restricts DNS/HTTP egress to allowlist only. We can provide a network diagram by EOD Thu 03/05 and we’ll fill your XLSX template.

Can you confirm whether Redwood Private supports CloudHSM-backed KMS during PoC, or if we should expect a staged integration where you run with envelope encryption first while KMS integration is validated? Also please confirm the list of IP ranges and ports we should expect to open for the PoC.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Kapoor
Director, Infra & Security | Mariner Health
samir.kapoor@marinerhealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

Samir —

Appreciate the quick response and clear answers. Short replies to your questions:

- CloudHSM: Redwood Private supports CloudHSM-backed KMS via our KMS integration layer; for the PoC we can run envelope encryption while we validate the direct HSM integration. Aditya will own the KMS onboarding and can share an integration checklist.
- Air-gap: quarterly model rollouts are fine; we’ll document the secure transfer workflow for emergency updates (we’ve done similar with other regulated customers).
- IP ranges & ports: attaching the matrix (redwood-private-overview.pdf includes the canonical egress/IP list). If your security team prefers, Dylan can join a short call to walk through the firewall rules.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Mariner: send network diagram + completed XLSX by Thu 03/05 (per Samir).
2) Redwood: Aditya to share KMS checklist and a PoC runbook by Fri 03/06.
3) Schedule infra deep-dive: propose Thu 03/11 10:00am ET — I’ll send a calendar invite if that works.

I attached the overview and the network template again for convenience. Happy to pair Dylan with your security team on the rule review.
